title: Require auth on risky legacy control paths and stop returning secrets
description: Keep legacy /api compatibility paths, but require authenticated access on risky config/task/provider flows and remove raw secret values from legacy config reads.
action: In backend/main.py, replace get_legacy_user() usage on /api/config, /api/tasks/{task_id}, /api/tasks/{task_id}/logs, /api/tasks/{task_id}/cancel, /api/build-site, /api/adjust-site, and /api/providers/{provider}/auth/* routes with Depends(get_current_user) or Depends(require_role(...)) as appropriate; keep response envelopes stable, but remove llm_api_key, codex_client_secret, and codex_access_token from the GET /api/config response body.

criteria: backend/main.py contains "async def get_config(current_user: object = Depends(get_current_user), db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db))"

backend/main.py contains "async def create_legacy_task(payload: dict[str, Any] = Body(default_factory=dict), current_user: object = Depends(require_role("developer")), db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db))"
convergence.definition_of_done: Legacy compatibility routes still exist, but risky control paths now require a real authenticated user and no longer leak provider secrets.

files.change: Require real current_user dependencies and remove secret fields from GET /api/config.
Reuse existing get_current_user/require_role helpers for legacy route protection without adding a new auth system.
Add tests for authenticated access and secret omission on legacy config/task/provider routes.

implementation: Update the exact legacy routes listed in the action field to accept current_user through existing auth dependencies instead of default-admin resolution.
Keep the route paths and non-secret response keys stable so legacy clients continue to function after authentication.
Sanitize GET /api/config so llm_api_key, codex_client_secret, and codex_access_token are omitted from the returned JSON.
Add focused pytest coverage that verifies anonymous requests fail and authenticated requests still receive the expected non-secret response shape.

success_metrics: Legacy config reads no longer expose provider secrets

rationale.chosen_approach: Tightening the risky legacy routes preserves compatibility while removing the most dangerous privileged shortcuts.
decision_factors: Returning raw secrets directly conflicts with trust and quality goals
rationale.tradeoffs: Legacy clients must authenticate, but route names and most response fields remain stable.

risks: Be careful not to remove unrelated low-risk legacy routes in the same change.
